commit.subject: feat(ledger): sync without T3 or codex app-server

entries.text: Addition from the coordinator, fold it into your plan: Codex's workspace-write sandbox blocks writes to .git (git commit fails with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: Operation not permitted'). So in CI the common pattern is: codex exec edits files, then a later workflow step commits. That commit has no 'git commit' action in any session. Support it: a commit with no matching commit action gets the session(s) in that worktree whose last activity ended before the commit time and after the previous commit's time, matched as 'session' (a third match kind, shown in the viewer like the others), whole session segment since the previous commit. Keep sha/time matches preferred. Cover it with a test, and document it in docs/production.md (CI section). Also: the <path> commits are being re-recorded right now; wait until 'git -C <path> log --oneline' shows the wordfreq commits before step 7.

For the fourth commit covering ledger features, I'm considering splitting out the push and hook functionality as a separate, more manageable concern since they're clearly separable from the core ledger logic. I'll strip out the publish/fetchRemote/hook pieces from the main files and tests, which should be doable by programmatically removing the relevant blocks.



I'll split commit 4 into two parts: first the session matching and clipping logic, then the `--push` flag and hook, staging intermediate versions of `Ledger.ts`, `ledgerCli.ts`, `core/ledger.ts`, and the test with push/hook code temporarily removed.

entries.text:
I realize the script is fragile — the filesystem is case-insensitive, so Ledger.ts and ledger.ts are colliding in the staging directory. I'll switch to distinct filenames and just handle the ledgerCli fixes manually instead of relying on the script.

I considered git worktrees but that gets messy with branch checkouts. The cleanest approach: save the final versions to a temp directory, trim the working files down to an intermediate state, run checks and commit, then restore the finals and commit again.



Since macOS's case-insensitive filesystem merged `Ledger.ts` and `ledger.ts` in staging, I'll save the final files, manually trim the working copies to the intermediate state, commit that, then restore the finals for the next commit.

feat(ledger): sync without T3 or codex app-server

`ledger sync` reads sessions from `--source auto|t3|codex-app-server|
codex-rollouts`, with `--codex-home`. auto takes T3 if its database exists
plus Codex rollout files; a missing T3 database or `codex` binary is not an
error, and the app-server starts only when asked for. With no T3 database
the app uses an empty thread store instead of failing.

A commit no `git commit` action made (the agent edits, a later CI step
commits, since Codex's sandbox blocks .git) goes to the session that ended
last between the previous commit and it, matched as "session"; SHA and time
matches still win.

Outputs are clipped to `--max-output` bytes (default 8192, head and tail,
0 keeps them); actions record the bytes cut and the viewer says so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
